paragraphs.title: Visions of Calamity and Appeals for Mercy

easy.explanation: Amos saw the Lord forming grasshoppers after the king’s mowings.
easy.q: What did Amos see in the first vision?

easy.explanation: Amos pleaded for Jacob, asking, “By whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small.”
easy.q: For whom did Amos plead for mercy?

easy.explanation: In the second vision, fire devoured the great deep and ate up a part.
easy.q: What was the calamity in the second vision?

medium.explanation: Amos based his appeal on the fact that Jacob was small.
medium.q: Why did Amos ask the Lord to forgive Jacob?

medium.explanation: The Lord relented, so the announced calamity would not take place.
medium.q: What does “repented” mean in “The LORD repented for this”?

medium.explanation: The Lord said that the disaster would not be.
medium.q: What happened after Amos’s request in the first vision?

answers: In both, Amos pleads for mercy and the Lord relents
The house of Jeroboam is destroyed in both
challenge.explanation: Both visions contain calamity, Amos’s appeal for Jacob, and the Lord’s decision to withhold that calamity.
challenge.q: What is similar about the first two visions?

answers: Amos announces that Jacob will conquer
challenge.explanation: The repeated words emphasize Jacob’s weakness and need for mercy.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the repeated words “By whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small”?

challenge.explanation: The grasshopper vision comes first with an appeal, followed by the fire vision and another appeal.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

paragraphs.title: The Plumb-Line Vision and the Decision of Judgment

answers: A wall made by a plumbline
easy.explanation: The Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline.
easy.q: What was the Lord standing upon in the third vision?
What did Amos see in the Lord’s hand?

answers: The Lord would rise against it with the sword
easy.explanation: The Lord declared, “I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
easy.q: What would happen to the house of Jeroboam?

medium.explanation: The Lord asked Amos, “What seest thou?”
medium.q: What did the Lord ask Amos in the vision?

answers: The Lord would no longer overlook their wrongdoing
The Lord would bless them again
The Lord would send them to rest
medium.explanation: The Lord announced that he would no longer pass over Israel’s wrongdoing.
medium.q: What does “I will not again pass by them any more” mean?

medium.explanation: The high places of Isaac would be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel would be laid waste.
medium.q: Which places were threatened with desolation and destruction?

challenge.explanation: The plumbline represents careful measurement and judgment of Israel.
challenge.q: What does the plumbline symbolize in this vision?

answers: The first calamities are withheld, but here judgment is declared
Amos sees nothing in the plumb-line vision
The house of Jeroboam appears in the first two visions
challenge.explanation: In the first two visions the Lord relents, but here he says he will no longer pass by Israel.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the first two visions and the plumb-line vision?

answers: The measurement shows that judgment and destruction are required
The wall represents the Lord’s mercy
challenge.explanation: After measuring Israel, the Lord announces the desolation of the high places, sanctuaries, and house of Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What connection is there between the plumbline and the destruction mentioned afterward?

paragraphs.title: Amos’s Confrontation with Amaziah and His Prophetic Mission

easy.explanation: Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent a report to Jeroboam.
Amaziah told Amos to flee into the land of Judah.
easy.q: Where did Amaziah tell Amos to go?

easy.explanation: Amos said that the Lord took him as he followed the flock.
easy.q: What was Amos doing before the Lord called him to prophesy?

answers: Because it was the king’s chapel and the king’s court
Because Amos wanted to be king
medium.explanation: Amaziah said that Bethel was the king’s chapel and the king’s court.
medium.q: Why did Amaziah tell Amos to leave Bethel?

answers: He was an herdman and a gatherer of sycomore fruit
medium.explanation: Amos said, “I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit.”
medium.q: What did Amos say about his occupation before his calling?

answers: He took Amos from his work and commanded him to prophesy
He appointed Amos priest at Bethel
medium.explanation: The Lord took Amos as he followed the flock and told him to prophesy to Israel.
medium.q: What did the Lord do according to Amos?

answers: Amaziah treats him as a wandering seer, while Amos emphasizes that he was a working man sent by the Lord
Amaziah treats him as a king, while Amos calls himself a priest
Amaziah calls him a shepherd, while Amos calls himself a soldier
challenge.explanation: Amaziah orders Amos to leave and prophesy elsewhere, while Amos explains that he was a working man whom the Lord called.
challenge.q: What is the difference between Amaziah’s view of Amos and Amos’s description of himself?

answers: Amaziah tries to silence him, while Amos says his authority comes from the Lord’s command
Amaziah asks for help, while Amos refuses
Amaziah offers him work, while Amos accepts it
challenge.explanation: Amaziah says, “Prophesy not,” but Amos declares that the Lord told him to prophesy.
challenge.q: What is the connection between Amaziah’s words and Amos’s response?

answers: Amaziah would die in a polluted land, and Israel would go into captivity
Amaziah would reign, and Israel would be restored
Amaziah would flee, and Israel would conquer
challenge.explanation: Amos announced that Amaziah would die in a polluted land and that Israel would surely go into captivity.
challenge.q: What punishment did Amos announce to Amaziah and Israel?
